entries.title: Notebooks & pages
entries.answer: Notebooks group pages of rich-text writing. Headings inside a page automatically become jump-able Topics, and pages can carry tags. Create a notebook from the Notebooks room, then “+ New page” inside it.

entries.title: Notebook legend
entries.answer: Each notebook has a Legend — its own cover/contents page, shown whenever nothing's open. It's reachable any time via the Legend button, either in the sidebar or right in a page's own toolbar, no matter how you got to that page.

entries.title: Topics
entries.answer: Topics are automatic: any heading you type in a page becomes a jump-able topic, listed under that page in the Legend. No separate step to create one.

entries.title: Tags
entries.answer: Tag a page from its toolbar. Tags get their own color and show up as small pills on the page, in lists, and in the Legend — useful for filtering and for sharpening Oracle's own matching if you teach it keyword-style entries.

entries.title: Timelines, epochs & eras
entries.answer: Timelines hold epochs, and epochs hold eras — each with a status, a summary, dated events, and its own page for writing it up. The Timelines room is where you build these out.

entries.title: Entries (characters, places, etc.)
entries.answer: Entries (characters, places, factions, and so on) aren't their own room — create and link them right from a page or timeline with the “+ Entry” button in the toolbar, so your world bible grows exactly where you're writing about it.

entries.title: Session timer
entries.answer: The timer lives in Productivity. Type what you're working on and hit Start; Stop logs it as a session. You can also log time you've already spent by hand, without running the timer, via “Log manually.”

entries.title: Pomodoro mode
entries.answer: Pomodoro alternates fixed work/break intervals automatically. Turn it on from the Pomodoro button next to the timer, where you can also set the work and break lengths in minutes. A finished work interval logs as a real session, same as stopping the timer manually.

entries.title: Weekly goals & tiers
entries.answer: Set an hours target for the week from Productivity's Goal card. Weeks get graded Met → Exceeded → Crushed → Legendary depending on how far over goal you land — each tier looks a little richer than the last. Here's where you stand right now:

entries.title: Rest days
entries.answer: Mark a day as rested from the timer card's “Take a rest day” button. Rest tokens are earned automatically and protect a week's streak without you needing to log any hours that day.

entries.title: Medals & prestige
entries.answer: Medals track streaks, total hours, goal weeks, and overachieving — each with the same Met/Exceeded/Crushed/Legendary tiers. Prestiging a medal after reaching Legendary resets its progress but keeps a badge with a color that cycles per prestige level; click a medal's “Pn” tag to see every prestige it's reached.

entries.title: Calendar & tasks
entries.answer: The Calendar (in Productivity) holds plans and tasks, one-off or recurring. A page's own Tasks panel and the Calendar's Tasks card share the same underlying list — a task linked to a page shows up in both places. Here's what's open right now:

entries.title: Recap
entries.answer: Recap (in Productivity) is a wrapped-style summary of a week, month, or year: an hours chart, quick stats, what pages/entries you actually created or built on, and an hours breakdown by project. Here it is, live:

entries.title: Management (budget & products)
entries.answer: Management tracks real-world accounts you set up yourself — a brokerage account, a side project, whatever — each holding its own earnings, expenses, and contributions, plus the products or deliverables you're building.

entries.title: Projects & switching
entries.answer: Each project is a separate world with its own notebooks/entries/timelines/management data. Productivity (calendar, timer, goals, medals) is shared across every project. Switch quickly via the rail button or Ctrl/Cmd+P.

entries.title: Export & import
entries.answer: Preferences → Data → “Export everything” backs up every project plus shared settings and Productivity data; Ctrl/Cmd+S does the same instantly. “Export this project” is scoped to just the current one. Import brings either back, and also reads old Suitebook exports.

entries.title: Snapshots
entries.answer: Preferences → Snapshots keeps automatic restore points for the current project, on an interval you control. They live in this browser, same as everything else — Export is the only copy that actually leaves it.

entries.title: Locking pages & Focus
entries.answer: Lock a page from its toolbar to stop it being edited or deleted by accident until unlocked. Focus (also in the toolbar) dims every paragraph but the one you're in.

entries.title: Feedback / bug reports
entries.answer: Preferences → Feedback opens a form for reporting a bug or suggesting an enhancement — pick which with the tabs at the top. It's reviewed and submitted on GitHub; nothing sends until you do.

entries.title: Checking for updates
entries.answer: Preferences → Check for updates compares your version against what's published. Version strings carry a channel (stable/beta/dev) as a suffix, shown as a colored tag, so you can tell a tested release from a build still in progress.

entries.title: Search & shortcuts
entries.answer: Ctrl/Cmd+K opens search. A few other shortcuts: Ctrl+N new page, Ctrl+B bold, Ctrl+S export everything.

entries.title: What Oracle can do
entries.answer: I can add a task (“remind me to outline chapter 3 tomorrow”), set your weekly goal (“set my goal to 12 hours”), or answer questions about how Notebook works.
